attrs.name: condition
attrs.description: The case this rule applies in: an expression over the owning entity's fields (the attr.expression grammar). Absent: always. The database CHECK is NOT (condition) OR (rule), so a row the condition does not hold for, or holds NULL for, is not checked. Enforced like the rule itself: by the database CHECK and, on create, by the generated record model in every port. Justified in ADR-0023 Amendment 1.

attrs.name: dbCheck
attrs.description: On a numeric, length or regex validator, false generates no database CHECK (meta migrate and a generated EF model leave it out); the generated app-level validators still enforce it on every write. On a cross-field validator (comparison, requiredWhen, presentIff, atLeastOne), which only its CHECK enforces, false is refused (ERR_CROSS_FIELD_WITHOUT_CHECK). Absent: true. For a column whose legacy rows break the rule, which a CHECK would refuse on their next UPDATE even NOT VALID. Refused with @constraintName (ERR_CONSTRAINT_NAME_WITHOUT_CHECK). sections.description: Cross-field ordering: requires two sibling fields of the owning entity stand in a relational order (@left @op @right), e.g. current_hp <= max_hp or expires_at > created_at. Entity-scoped; references fields by name. Backends derive the rule (CHECK constraint, cross-field assertion) — no raw expression is stored.
sections.rules: @left and @right must name fields of the owning entity. @op is one of gt/gte/lt/lte/ne/eq. The comparison is null-tolerant where the backend's relational operator is (SQL: a NULL operand yields no violation).
sections.whenToUse: Two sibling fields must stand in an order (start <= end, currentHp <= maxHp). Declare it instead of hand-writing the cross-field assertion.

sections.description: Biconditional presence: the target field (@field) is present (NOT NULL) if and only if the gating field (@when) equals @equals. Models paired flag/companion-column invariants, e.g. used_at present iff is_used=true. Entity-scoped; references fields by name.
